the development of efficient and effective deep 3D CNN architectures for medical image analysis and the application of our pipeline to the challenging task of multi class brain lesion segmentation.

the proposed network architecture is the first to achieve state of the art segmentation performance on three challenging tasks in brain lesion segmentation while at the same time being computationally efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel and efficient 3D CNN for the task of brain lesion detection and segmentation.
our proposed architecture is a computationally efficient, state of the art performing, deep 3D CNN for the challenging task brain lesion segmentation.

the presented approach is the first 3D CNN based method for lesion segmentation that achieves state of the art performance while being computationally efficient enough to allow for its adoption in clinical settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D CNN architectures are able to learn discriminative features at multiple scales and are able to outperform their 2D counterparts in the task of brain lesion detection.
the proposed architecture is able to learn a rich representation of the underlying data that allows for accurate lesion delineation, even in the absence of large amounts of annotated data.
the proposed architecture is capable of automatically learning intermediate feature representations that are both discriminative and interpretable.
